title: The Trail of the Empty Quarter
premise: Felix Whitlock flies medicine and gossip into the northern interior, haunted by an expedition ten years ago that came back one man short and sworn to silence. When his old rival Dara Okonkwo arrives with money and a map, she hires Felix and his crew to retrace that lost route before the monsoon seals the high country — officially to recover a downed survey plane, actually to find what the first expedition buried. What they find is proof that Felix's missing partner survived, lived among the valley people, and died protecting a secret worth killing for: a mineral strike that three parties will burn the forest to own. Betrayed from within by their own financier's agent, the crew must choose between selling the truth or destroying it; in the end Felix burns the evidence, gives the valley's location to no one, and brings his people home through the monsoon's first wall of rain — poorer, fewer, and finally free of the past.
about_author: Astrid Voss is a former bush pilot who logged six years on supply runs across subarctic lakes before trading her headset for a keyboard. She writes adventure fiction from a cabin she refuses to locate precisely.

chapters.title: Fuel, Ice, and Rumors
chapters.summary: Felix Whitlock's POV. A routine medevac run introduces the crew — mechanic June, loadmaster Cole, rookie navigator Sami — and the fragile economy keeping their operation alive. A letter arrives bearing a signature Felix hasn't seen in ten years. The beat is uneasy nostalgia: the past knocking politely before it kicks the door.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Left
chapters.summary: Dara Okonkwo arrives at the float base with a contract, a satellite map, and an apology Felix doesn't want. Flashback fragments reveal the expedition that ended with Tom Reyes walking into the mist and never coming back. POV alternates Felix and Dara. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened under fluorescent hangar lights.

chapters.title: Crew Meeting
chapters.summary: June's POV. The crew debates the job: triple pay, monsoon deadline, and a route Felix has forbidden on the charts for a decade. Cole wants the money; Sami smells a lie; June watches Felix crack for the first time since she's known him. They vote yes. Beat: loyalty chosen over instinct, the first domino.

chapters.title: Weight and Balance
chapters.summary: Sami's POV. Preparations expose cracks: Dara insists on bringing her quiet 'geologist' Marek, whose gear list includes things geologists don't carry. A customs officer asks pointed questions about their flight plan. Beat: dread disguised as logistics; the reader sees the trap being assembled.

chapters.title: North of the Last Lake
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The flight in, weather deteriorating, terrain growing hostile. Dara navigates from memory she claims she shouldn't have. They land on a strip that appears on no chart but is clearly man-made. Beat: crossing the threshold — the wilderness stops being scenery and becomes a character with opinions.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: June's POV while Felix scouts upstream. They find the wreck of the 'survey plane' — shot down, not crashed, and ten years older than Dara claimed. Marek photographs everything too carefully. Beat: the mission's cover story dies quietly in the alder brush.

chapters.title: Dara's Version
chapters.summary: Dara's POV, finally honest with the reader if not the crew: she was on the original expedition, she loved Tom Reyes, and she believes he survived and stayed. Her real goal is a grave, not a mine. Beat: sympathy complicates suspicion — the rival becomes human.

chapters.title: Smoke Where Smoke Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Sami's POV. On night watch, Sami spots a fire in the high valley and wakes the camp. Someone is living up there. Marek makes a satellite call when he thinks everyone sleeps. Beat: the hunted feeling begins; the forest has witnesses.

chapters.title: The Valley People
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Contact: a small community descended from trappers and the expedition's abandoned guides, led by an elder named Ilsa who recognizes Felix's surname and spits. She knows exactly who they are and why they've come. Beat: judgment from outside the law — the valley remembers what the world forgot.

chapters.title: Tom's Cabin
chapters.summary: June's POV. Ilsa leads them to a cabin: Tom Reyes lived here twenty years, married into the community, and died two winters ago defending it from prospectors. His journal details a mineral strike he deliberately mischarted to keep it hidden. Beat: grief arriving late, and the terrible weight of a friend's long life without you.

chapters.title: Marek Moves
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. Marek steals the journal pages and radios his employer — a mining consortium that funded Dara without her full knowledge. Cole catches him mid-theft; a scuffle leaves Marek injured and the radio destroyed. Beat: betrayal made physical; now there's a body to carry and a clock that just sped up.

chapters.title: The Consortium
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Interrogating the wounded Marek, they learn a corporate retrieval team is already inbound by helicopter, and Dara realizes her backers used her grief as a hunting license. Her fury turns against her own paymasters. Beat: rage as clarity — the enemy finally has a face.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Law
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The valley people put the question to them: leave the strike secret and be welcome, or carry it out and never return. Ilsa reveals the prospectors' earlier visit ended in a death the outside world never investigated. Beat: justice outside the law — the crew must accept a verdict no court will ever hear.

chapters.title: Splitting the Load
chapters.summary: June's POV. The plane can't lift everyone plus fuel plus the coming storm. They cache supplies, rig the wreck site to look undisturbed, and plan a deception for the incoming team. Sami volunteers for the riskiest leg. Beat: competence under pressure; family forged by shared danger.

chapters.title: Helicopters at Dawn
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. The retrieval team arrives — four men, armed, polite, led by a fixer named Vossen who offers to buy the crew's silence and then their lives. Felix stalls while June and Sami move the plane. Beat: cold menace; the price of survival gets quoted in cash and blood.

chapters.title: The Runway Fight
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Vossen's men seize the strip; a desperate night action — flares, fuel fires, Cole taking a bullet in the shoulder — drives them off but wrecks the plane's landing gear. Beat: the cost comes due; heroism here is ugly, improvised, and expensive.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Sami's POV. With the plane crippled and monsoon clouds stacking on the horizon, the only way out is Tom's old route: river, portage, and a derelict boat below the falls. Ilsa's people offer canoes and a guide — her grandson, Ansel. Beat: humility; salvation comes from the people they once wrote off.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: June's POV. The descent — rapids, a capsized canoe, fever setting into Cole's wound. Dara proves herself carrying gear through the portage, earning what apology couldn't. Beat: endurance as love language; the crew stops being employees and becomes kin.

chapters.title: Vossen Catches Up
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Vossen's remaining men ambush them at the falls. In the confrontation, Felix chooses not to kill the helpless Vossen but strips the team's evidence, maps, and satellite phone and lets the river take them — and nearly takes Dara. Beat: the climax's moral hinge; mercy as the harder choice.

chapters.title: The Burning Page
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. At the last camp, Dara reads Tom's final journal entry — addressed to whoever came looking — asking them to let the valley keep its secret. She burns the strike data herself, weeping, while Felix stands witness. Beat: catharsis; truth weighed against loyalty, and loyalty winning at last.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The monsoon hits as they reach the coastal station — a whiteout arrival, Cole stretchered to a clinic, the crew telling officials a clean, boring story about a failed survey. Vossen's drowned equipment supports it. Beat: survival's anticlimax; the greatest lie is that nothing happened.

chapters.title: The Trail Ahead
chapters.summary: June's POV, weeks later. The base rebuilt, Cole mending, Sami promoted, Dara gone but leaving behind Tom's compass and a note: 'Some trails are meant to stay empty.' Felix files a new flight plan north — not to the valley, but toward it, carrying medicine and nothing else. Beat: quiet resolution; forgiveness earned, secrets kept, the wilderness still forgiving nothing and forgetting less.
